# The `vendor` Directory

This is the odd directory of MicrobeTrace dependencies that can't be bundled. for the Javascripts, this is probably because we need accessible to `importScripts` in Workers. For others, it's probably because of some CSS relative path shenanigans.

The version of each library here (and in `dist/`) is recorded in `dist/versions.json`, which `scripts/bundle.js` writes.

Either way, the contents of this directory are generated by copying stuff out of the `node_modules` directory (`npm run bundle`), and **those generated files are not committed** (they are gitignored, as are `dist/` and `fonts/`). CI, the Docker build and the Pages deploy build them, and `npm start` builds them when they are missing or out of date. Only this README and the bx-distance-models build below are committed, because that build is not on NPM in a loadable form.

## bx-distance-models

`bx_distance_models.js` and `bx_distance_models_bg.wasm` are the WebAssembly build of
[bx-distance-models](https://github.com/AABoyles/bx-distance-models), the engine that
`workers/compute-links.js` uses to compute genetic distances (TN93, TN92, K2P, JC69, SNPs,
Hamming, p-distance, transitions, transversions and Ts/Tv ratio). Its NPM package is an ES module,
which workers can't load with `importScripts`, so rebuild it from a checkout with
`scripts/build-bx.sh path/to/bx-distance-models` (needs Rust with the `wasm32-unknown-unknown`
target and `wasm-pack`). The committed build is from commit `970bba4` (0.2.0, bx-distance-models
PR #8, tn93 parity; built with Rust 1.100.0 and wasm-pack 0.15.1). It implements every ambiguity
mode of HIV-TRACE's `tn93 -a` (skip, resolve, average and GapMM, with `N` and `?` compared as any
base), and its `-g` maximum ambiguity fraction, so MicrobeTrace no longer needs tn93.js. Since
`39f47f3` it implements TN92 as Tamura (1992) (3cb2ca9), no longer caps corrected distances at 1
(they can exceed 1, or be `Infinity` when the model saturates, with no Hamming fallback), and
returns `NaN` rather than 1 for a pair with no comparable sites. Consumers of distances have to
tolerate both.

## cosmos.gl

`cosmos.min.js` is a build of [cosmos.gl](https://github.com/cosmosgl/graph) (`@cosmos.gl/graph`
3.6.0, MIT), which lays out and draws the 2D network on the GPU. `components/network.html` loads
it the first time that view opens. `scripts/bundle.js` builds it from `node_modules` unpatched: since
3.6 cosmos.gl shifts the many-body force's grid every tick itself, which the earlier local patch did.
